newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end just firmer in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end just firmer in cautious trade.

text.p: SPI Futures cl 2479 +2 US 30yr cl 7.08 +0.04
10yrbond futs 92.110 -0.050 Gold NY 341.35 Lon fix 341.00
AUD US$0.7746 (Wed 0.7778) CRB Index cl 246.85 +0.31
*Stocks ended just firm on option-boosted volume in cautious trade ahead of the ANZAC Day long weekend. Volume 301.6 million, value A$752.3 million, 1,055 traded, 287 steady, 390 up, 378 down.
Australian shares finished slightly firmer on Thursday in quiet trade ahead of the ANZAC Day long weekend with local investors reluctant to take positions ahead of two Wall Street sessions.
Australian markets will be closed on Friday for ANZAC Day.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed up 2.4 points at 2,474.7, after touching an intra-day high of 2,480.2.
June share price index futures finished up two points at 2,479, a 4.3 point premium to the index.
A reasonable proportion of the day's volume was generated by today's April series option expiries.
"Some players were holding stocks up for the option exercises - that's always a factor on the afternoon of the option exercise," said Scott Healy, a dealer at Brisbane broker Wilson HTM.
Healy said there could have been more interest in the market today if it had not been the day before a long weekend.
"It was a funny day. I think people were a bit hesistant because they have the day off tomorrow," he said.
Healy said he estimated about 10 percent of the turnover was related to option expiries.
Among the oustanding stocks on the day was fertiliser and chemical manufacturer Incitec Ltd whose shares closed 24 cents higher at A$6.34 after reporting a steady profit result for its first half.
Beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd also had a good session, and dealers said its stock has a tendency to jump around due to the relative shortage of scrip.
Coca-Cola Amatil shares ended 47.7 cents higher at A$15.20 on turnover of 692,522 shares.
The number of stocks rising was approximately equal to the number falling with about a third of issues traded steady.

In other local markets, Australian bond yield spreads showed a widening bias against its dollar bloc partners, extending Wednesday's blow-out following a set of inflation data that did not live up to the most optimistic expectations.
The yield on 10 year T-bonds closed at 7.87 percent, up 0.04 percentage points from Wednesday's close.

The Australian dollar had another indecisive session as failures in both directions offshore reinforced the strength of the recent range. By 4.45 p.m (0645 GMT), the local dollar had drifted to US$0.7743/48 from US$0.7777/82 late here Wednesday, and was still stuck in the week's US$0.7730/7795 range.
